crime_highlights: She died, as found by the jury, at the hands of the appellant.
The cause of Isabella's death was blunt force trauma to the abdomen which ruptured her mesentery vein and caused internal bleeding.
he punched Isabella in her stomach on the night in question and had done so approximately 25 times in the past
Mr. Sunshine also said that he burned Isabella.
rationale_highlights: intergenerational effects of attendance at the residential school attended by members of Mr. Sunshine's aboriginal community
connecting Gladue considerations concerning systemic and commonly experienced effects of aboriginal background to Mr. Sunshine
but for Mr. Sunshine's aboriginal status and own deprived background, would have supported a longer period of parole ineligibility than was accorded Mr. Sunshine
The new Gladue report makes the shocking abuse of Mr. Sunshine as a child even more clear
the judge adequately reflected these aspects of the case by applying a parole ineligibility period at the lowest point of the range he settled on for the offence
note: Majority (Saunders J.A.) own view: background lowered parole ineligibility.

crime_highlights: the appellant committed aggravated assault by using a knife to slash the face of an acquaintance
Within five seconds of Mr. Olson exiting the McDonalds, the appellant approached him, slashed his face, and walked away.
Mr. Olson required emergency surgery and was left with lasting damage to his facial nerves.
rationale_highlights: including serious childhood neglect and abuse, and substance abuse, related to his very disadvantaged upbringing
The judge observed the pre-sentence report was thorough and addressed the Gladue factors and Aboriginal background of Mr. Brennan, which the judge reviewed and considered.
He found the Gladue factors, the mitigating factor of the guilty pleas, and the prospects of rehabilitation all to be relevant.
note: Credit-only appeal; court never states Gladue factors reduced the sentence.

crime_highlights: Mr. Townsend punches Ms. Litzen-Parson in the head with the result that she falls to the ground
Mr. Townsend responds by punching Mr. Riley in the head, dropping him to the ground.
Mr. Riley lies motionless and apparently unconscious on the street in front of a running car.
Mr. Townsend forcefully and brutally stomps on Mr. Riley's head.
Mr. Riley suffered ongoing concussive symptoms, a fracture to his cheekbone, a non-displaced fracture of his nose and two broken teeth.
Mr. Rafiq lost a front tooth and also had a concussion and a non-displaced fracture of his nose.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Townsend is of aboriginal heritage and had suffered some hardship in his life, including losing his mother at age 16, losing his sister and losing a number of close friends.
the sentencing judge stood back and referred in particular to Mr. Townsend's Aboriginal status
she did step back, referred to totality, considered that the 48 months was inappropriate, and made a significant adjustment
note: Appeal court frames reduction as totality; never adopts Aboriginal status as mitigating.
